newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRB Group liabilities seen at 9.3 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India CRB Group liabilities seen at 9.3 bln rupees.

text.p: India's Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has estimated the failed CRB Group of companies' liabilities at 9.32 billion rupees, CBI director Joginder Singh said on Friday.

This includes CRB group companies' liabilities to banks, the Gujarat state government, participants of the inter-corporate deposit market and the public who invested deposits in flagship CRB Capital Markets Ltd and in the group's mutual fund, Singh told a news conference.
CRB Capital Markets, with 14 offices spread across the country, was last week charged with a series of irregularities by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
Singh, is in Bombay to coordinate investigations into CRB Capital Markets against whom a winding up petition has been filed by the RBI in the Delhi High Court.
He said investigations are expected to be completed in one month's time.

A committee with representatives from the CBI, Maharashtra state police, the revenue and income tax departments, the RBI and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has been set up to expedite investigations, he said.
Investigations are spearheaded by Arup Patnaik, CBI's deputy inspector general in charge of banking and finance frauds, CBI officials said.
"We will conduct impartial investigations," Singh said. "There is no pressure on CBI from any quarter."
